Mr Liang Eng Hwa
New and enhanced enterprise schemes

The Finance Minister introduced new schemes, extended existing ones, and streamlined eight ESG financing schemes into a single Enterprise Financing Scheme.

  2. s00003Mr Liang Eng Hwa — Holland-Bukit Timah

    Besides new schemes, such as Scale‐up SG, Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) Co‐Investment Fund III and the Innovation Agent Programme, the Finance Minister has also extended and enhanced existing schemes, such as the Enterprise Development Grant (EDG), the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) and others, with the intent to boost effectiveness and reap better outcomes.

  3. s00004Mr Liang Eng Hwa — Holland-Bukit Timah

    Eight existing financing schemes offered by Enterprise Singapore (ESG) were also streamlined into a single Enterprise Financing Scheme (EFS), making it simpler for businesses to apply and easier to access the loans.

Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
Calibrating policies for seniors

The speaker proposes calibrating healthcare, manpower, pension, housing and gender policies so seniors age with independence, listing five specific measures.

  1. s01319Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong — Non-Constituency Membercontext

    I have made the case that: one, CHAS auto-enrollment and outpatient subsidies should kick in for all Singaporeans who turn 60 years old to plug the primary care gap in our universal healthcare system; two, the retirement age be removed, the redefined re-employment age raised to 70 years old and the CPF contribution for older workers restored so that our seniors can continue working as long as they can and want; three, CPF be transformed into a safety net for seniors, that payout eligibility age be lowered to 60 years old and members be allowed to make partial withdrawals if incapacitated to work for a period of time; four, ageing in place be deepened by promoting the Lease Buyback Scheme to the Merdekas; and five, close the gender gap in CPF and other savings for our senior women by increasing the MediSave top-ups for them and the participation incentive for them to enrol in CareShield Life.

  3. s01321Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong — Non-Constituency Member

Five proposals for seniors

Five proposals cover automatic CHAS and outpatient treatment at 60, abolishing retirement age and raising re-employment to 70, lowering CPF withdrawal age to 60, promoting Lease Buyback for the Merdeka Generation, and MediSave top-ups for female seniors.

  1. s01679Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap — Aljunied

    First, automatic registration for CHAS subsidies and also outpatient treatment for all Singaporeans once they reach 60 years old.

  3. s01681Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap — Aljunied

    Second, abolish the retirement age, increase the re-employment age to 70 and restore the CPF contributions for older workers so that our seniors can continue to work as long as they wish to and are able to.

  4. s01682Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap — Aljunied

    Third, transform the CPF into a safety net for seniors whereby the eligible withdrawal age, or the age when they are eligible to receive payouts, is lowered to 60 and members are allowed to make partial withdrawals from the available sum if they are unable to work for a certain period of time due to health issues.

  5. s01683Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap — Aljunied

    Fourth, strengthen ageing further by promoting HDB's Lease Buyback Scheme to the Merdeka Generation.

  6. s01684Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap — Aljunied

    Fifth and finally, address the gender gap for CPF and other savings for our female seniors by increasing the amount of MediSave top-ups for this group and also provide incentives for participation so that they will register for CareShield Life.

Cross-cultural literacy defined

Cross-cultural literacy is the ability to understand and interact across cultures sensitively and respectfully of diversity.

    Cross-cultural literacy is the ability to understand and interact across different cultures in a manner that is sensitive to differences, yet respectful of diversity.

  3. s01714Prof Lim Sun Sun — Nominated Membercontext

    However, we must be vigilant about any emerging digital skills divides that may find certain segments of our population less advantaged and less able to benefit from our digitalisation push.

  6. s01717Prof Lim Sun Sun — Nominated Member

Prof Lim Sun Sun

Growing digitalisation requires enhancing the workforce's ethical literacy to recognise and resolve ethical issues.

  1. s01725Prof Lim Sun Sun — Nominated Member

  3. s01727Prof Lim Sun Sun — Nominated Member

    In this regard, we must vest our workforce with the competencies to recognise ethical issues where and when they present themselves, understand different ethical perspectives and to apply these perspectives to help resolve ethical conundrums.

Big Tech ethical controversies

Big Tech controversies show inattention to ethics causes problems, making the Proposed Model AI Governance Framework farsighted and commendable.

  2. s01732Prof Lim Sun Sun — Nominated Member

    In this regard, the Proposed Model AI Governance Framework launched in January is both farsighted and commendable.

In my Budget Debate speech last year, I said that while I support the push for digitalisation and innovation under the Sea Transport ITM, we must not forget those who may not be able to benefit from this development.

    (a) Introduction of CHAS to allow Singaporeans to enjoy subsidies at private general practitioner (GP) and dental clinics for treatment and screening; (b) Introduction of the PGP and now the $ 6.1 billion MGP, and the upcoming Elderfund scheme, to support Singaporeans who are severely disabled; (c) Substantial increase in subsidies offered to lower- and middle-income patients for long-term care services, specialist care and medications; (d) MediShield Life and the new CareShield Life as universal healthcare insurance to ensure lifetime coverage and higher monthly payouts; (e) Expansion of aged care services, such as home care services, eldercare centres and nursing homes, to cater for the needs of our ageing population; (f) Ramping up of healthcare facilities and infrastructure with at least one hospital built every two years, and strengthening of healthcare worker numbers and capabilities; (g) Implementing the MOH's Community Network for Seniors scheme that links seniors who live alone with befrienders and volunteers, and help them with social problems and early referral of complex needs to MOH.
